body:
## Symptom

After a sample or site is edited, its numbers in Fuseki change type from `xsd:decimal` to `xsd:double`, so Fuseki shows them in exponent form: `1.25` becomes `1.25e0`. The old decimal values aren't removed. They stay in the store on orphaned nodes that nothing links to anymore.

## Evidence (dev Fuseki, 2026-10-01)

- About 1.5M numeric literals are `xsd:decimal`. Only 73 are `xsd:double`, and all of those come from the one edited sample (Ono 2004 kawazulite) and its CandidateEntities.
- 13 orphaned `:Element` nodes still have a `:grade`, and no `:Analysis` points to them. Each holds exactly one triple, e.g. `gcr:Element_2c61ba3d_… :grade "1.25"^^xsd:decimal`. Their values match the live kawazulite grades: 0.04, 0.05, 0.06, 1.25, 8.54, 29.33, 61.5.
- 24 orphaned `CandidateEntity` nodes still hold a decimal `:confidence`.

```sparql
SELECT ?e (STR(?g) AS ?lex) (datatype(?g) AS ?dt) WHERE {
  ?e <https://geochemistry.isi.edu/ontology/grade> ?g
  FILTER NOT EXISTS { ?a <https://geochemistry.isi.edu/ontology/element> ?e }
}
```

## Cause

In `minmodkg/services/sync/kgsync_listener.py` (`handle_sample_update` and `handle_site_update`):

1. Nested nodes (Analysis, Element, CandidateEntity, …) get a fresh `uuid4` URI on every `to_kg()` (`libraries/rdf/rdf_model.py`). So every edit deletes and re-inserts the whole nested tree, not just the field that changed.
2. Before diffing, both the old and new triples go through `norm_literal()` (`misc/utils.py`). It rewrites every decimal/float/double as `xsd:double`; according to its docstring, it was written for Virtuoso, which reads decimals back as doubles.
3. The DELETE is built from those rewritten triples. It asks Fuseki to remove `"1.25"^^xsd:double`, but the store holds `"1.25"^^xsd:decimal`. Fuseki treats them as different values, so nothing is deleted. Text, boolean and URI triples match and are removed, which leaves the numeric triple stranded on a node nothing links to.
4. The INSERT also uses the rewritten triples, so the new values land as `xsd:double` (the `e0` form) instead of `xsd:decimal` like the rest of the data.

## Impact

- Every edit leaves dead triples behind, and they pile up over time.
- Anything that queries grades or confidences without going through the parent nodes (counts, averages, value searches) also picks up the stale values.
- Edited and unedited data end up with different datatypes.
- `handle_site_update` uses the same logic, so ordinary MinMod mineral-site edits likely do the same thing in prod. Not checked yet: prod Fuseki only listens on localhost.

## Fix

- Use `norm_literal` only to compare old and new. Build the DELETE from the original terms read back from the store, and the INSERT from the model's own terms (`xsd:decimal`).
- Optional: give nested nodes stable URIs (e.g. derived from the parent plus a key) so an edit only touches what changed.
- Cleanup: delete subjects of type Element/Analysis/CandidateEntity that nothing points to, after reviewing what the query matches first.
title: KG sync leaves orphaned numeric triples after every edit (decimal vs. double mismatch)
